findings: Defect chain re-checked at 6aed33aad. BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim (server/internal/service/task_knowledge.go:392-403) binds the descriptor to the chosen native session: either the existing binding from taskKnowledgeResume, or binding.NativeSessionID=chosen. finalizeTaskKnowledgeClaim (557-608) stores that descriptor. runTask then calls StartTask, and after that gateResumeToReachableSession (server/internal/daemon/daemon.go:5908-5937, called at ~7587). On a missing workdir, a different workdir or an unreachable session home, the gate clears task.PriorSessionID and sets PriorSessionResumeUnavailable. gateCodexResumeToRolloutPresence (daemon.go:6082-6099) is a second drop site, but it applies only to Codex.

validateKnowledgeClaim (server/internal/daemon/knowledge_context.go:226) requires d.Session.NativeSessionID == opts.ResumeSessionID == task.PriorSessionID. After a drop that check refuses with knowledge_context_changed. runTask returns Status "blocked" (daemon.go:7911-7914) with zero prepare calls and zero processes.

A fresh launch is also impossible on the server today. PrepareTaskKnowledge requires req.Session == c.Descriptor.Session (task_knowledge_prepare.go:381), and Authorize requires the same (494). The agent package refuses a Resume intent whose ResumeSessionID is empty (pkg/agent/knowledge_launch.go:194-196). Both strict decoders reject any new request field with 400 invalid_knowledge_request: the handler's decodeTaskKnowledgeRequest uses DisallowUnknownFields, and so does protocol UnmarshalJSON via decodeKnowledgeObject. The daemon maps that 400 to knowledge_unavailable (knowledge_context.go:195-204) because invalid_knowledge_request is not in knowledgeFailureCode.

Why it repeats: the blocked row keeps session_id NULL, and GetLastTaskSession keeps choosing the stale row. Chat uses its chat_session pointer, which does not advance either. Nothing retires the stale session, because the deferred RetiredSessionID setter is registered only after prepareKnowledgePrompt (daemon.go ~7951). FailTask already COALESCEs retired_session_id (agent.sql:1415), but the blocked path never sets it.

Rewriting the claimed descriptor before its first preparation relabels no exposure. Exposure is recorded only when c.Prepared is set (task_knowledge_prepare.go:433) and on attempts. ListTaskKnowledgeHistory (pkg/db/queries/task_knowledge.sql:3-12) and taskKnowledgeExposure (task_knowledge.go:481-541) match a claim only by its descriptor NativeSessionID or an attempt's BoundSessionID. A rebound claim (descriptor native "", BoundSessionID = new ID) therefore never matches the stale native ID, and the stale session's earlier rows keep their exposure byte for byte.

decodeTaskKnowledge (task_knowledge.go:92-114) accepts a rebound claim. A claimed phase must have no attempts, and every later Authorization.Session must equal Descriptor.Session, which is the fresh binding when the rebind happens before any attempt. No new persisted field is needed, so an older server decodes rebound rows unchanged.

TaskKnowledgeRequestHash marshals the request struct (pkg/protocol/task_knowledge.go:207-213). A new `omitempty` bool keeps the hash of every unflagged request byte-identical, so original prepare receipts recorded before an upgrade still replay after it.

Existing coverage: TestKnowledgeActualResumeKeepsExactScopeGeneration (server/internal/daemon/knowledge_context_claim_test.go:267-298) reuses first.WorkDir, which still exists. No daemon, service or handler test pairs an unreachable prior workdir with a knowledge descriptor. TestTaskKnowledgeRequestRejectsPrivateOrAmbiguousFields keeps passing after the fix because its unknown-field case uses candidate_id.

Pre-existing residual risk, outside H2 and not widened by the fix: a Fresh intent binds any observed native ID (knowledge_launch.go:247-248; task_knowledge_observe.go:183-188). A compromised daemon that resumes outside ExecOptions could therefore bind an old native ID under a new generation. The next BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim fails safe to fresh, because the generations disagree (task_knowledge.go:528).
root_cause: The server binds the claim's knowledge descriptor to the chosen native session at claim time. Only after claim and StartTask can the daemon find out whether that session can be reached. The daemon's reachability gates then turn the turn into a fresh session. The legacy path accepts that. The knowledge path has no way to tell the server, and three exact-equality checks treat the post-gate state as a stale claim and refuse it: the daemon's validateKnowledgeClaim, the server's prepare/authorize `req.Session == descriptor` comparison, and the agent package's Resume-intent check. The refused attempt never publishes a session_id and never retires the stale one, so the next claim's chooser returns the same unreachable session and every later input on that issue or chat fails the same way.

alternatives.name: (a) Rebind at first preparation (resume_unavailable flag)
alternatives.summary: When a gate drops the bound native session, the daemon sends the original claimed session plus `resume_unavailable:true` on prepare. Only before the claim's first disclosure, the server replaces the descriptor session with a new generation and an empty native ID in the same transaction. It resolves current knowledge fresh and returns the fresh binding. The daemon checks that only generation and native ID changed, then launches fresh with the ordinary continuity notice. Authorize and observe go through the unchanged paths.
alternatives.pros: The rebind commits atomically with disclosure: a busy or failed transaction rolls back both, so there is no intermediate state. The fresh session gets the current manifest under the existing lock graph, per-attempt authorization and atomic native binding. No exposure is relabeled. No persisted field is added, so a server rollback stays safe. Unflagged request hashes do not change. The same turn continues with the legacy notice. About 60-80 production lines across protocol, service and daemon.
alternatives.cons: The server cannot verify the daemon's reachability claim, but the claim grants nothing beyond what any fresh claim of the task gets. An older server rejects the field (400, reported as knowledge_unavailable), which fails closed. An old daemon still fails until upgraded. The prepare replay branch needs a special case because the descriptor changes.

alternatives.name: (b) Resume-unsafe failure plus server-side skip
alternatives.summary: The daemon fails the turn with a new reason (e.g. knowledge_resume_unavailable) and reports RetiredSessionID. FailTask already stores retired_session_id and GetLastTaskSession excludes retired sessions, so the next claim skips the stale session. Optionally the server requeues the input.
alternatives.pros: No prepare protocol change; reuses the existing retired_session_id column and filter; old servers already accept retired_session_id.
alternatives.cons: The current input still fails. Without auto-retry the user must resend, which is worse than the legacy notice. Auto-retry contradicts the spec rule that knowledge failure reasons are excluded from automatic fresh fallback, requeue and input replay, and would need a new requeue path. Retirement is permanent, so a transient cause permanently discards a good session: a sibling's workdir lock, local_directory, an unmounted Hermes store. The chooser then falls back to an older session that may also be unreachable, costing another input each time. Needs a new failure reason in knowledgeFailureCode, the taxonomy, the docs and the UI.

alternatives.name: (c) Report reachable prior sessions in the claim body
alternatives.summary: The daemon lists the prior workdirs/sessions it can reach in each claim request. The server chooser picks only from that list before binding the descriptor.
alternatives.pros: Moves the decision before binding, so the descriptor is right from the start.
alternatives.cons: The daemon does not know which task it will receive, so it must list every local session, an unbounded list that exposes local inventory to the server. Reachability depends on decisions made after the claim: shouldReusePriorWorkdir, local_directory assignment, sibling workdir locks, the Hermes/pi store mount and Codex rollout presence. It cannot be computed at claim time. GC between claim and gate (TOCTOU) means (a) or (b) is still needed as a backstop. All three claim transports (single, batch, WS) change. Largest change.

alternatives.name: (d) Separate rebind endpoint before prepare
alternatives.summary: A new POST .../knowledge-context/rebind rewrites the descriptor, then the ordinary prepare follows.
alternatives.cons: Adds a new route, auth wiring, an idempotency receipt and a persisted intermediate state (rebound but not prepared), plus a round trip. A rebind can commit and the prepare then fail. Older servers return 404, so compatibility is no better than (a). Same trust model with more code.

chosen: (a) Rebind at first preparation: an optional `resume_unavailable` field on TaskKnowledgePrepareRequest, validated and applied by PrepareTaskKnowledge in the same transaction that discloses.
rationale: Option (a) is the only one that keeps the user's turn running in the same attempt while every launch still goes through prepare, authorize and observe. That matches the legacy notice behavior and needs no replay or requeue, which the spec forbids for knowledge failures. The rebind is limited to a claim with no preparation and no attempts, so it cannot move recorded exposure. The stale session's rows are untouched and still go through revalidation in BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim if that session is ever chosen again. It also commits or rolls back together with disclosure, so a knowledge_busy rollback leaves the original claim intact. The trust cost is small. The server cannot check reachability, but a daemon that says 'unreachable' gets a fresh generation, which is what the server's own chooser already hands out whenever revalidation fails. Option (b) costs every affected input and permanently retires sessions over transient causes. Option (c) cannot know reachability at claim time and still needs a backstop. Option (d) does the same as (a) with more surface and a non-atomic intermediate state.

changes.change: Add `ResumeUnavailable bool `json:"resume_unavailable,omitempty"`` as the last field of TaskKnowledgePrepareRequest. Keep UnmarshalJSON's required list unchanged: the field is optional, and checkCollaborationHostJSONFields accepts declared fields and still rejects case aliases. Do not change the response type; its `session` field carries the fresh binding.

(1) PrepareTaskKnowledge prevalidation (~361): `req.ResumeUnavailable && req.Session.NativeSessionID == ""` returns 400 invalid_knowledge_request. (2) taskKnowledgeTransaction gains a `rebind bool` parameter (Prepare passes req.ResumeUnavailable, Authorize passes false). Compute `session := c.Descriptor.Session; if rebind && c.Prepared == nil { session.NativeSessionID = "" }`, both from the pre-read claim and again from the in-transaction claim. Use it for the pre-tx exposure (137), the in-tx exposure (330) and the binding comparison (334), so stale-session history is neither locked nor revalidated for a turn that will not see it. (3) In Prepare's fn, replace the single `req.Session != c.Descriptor.Session` check (381) with three branches. Branch A (flagged, c.Prepared == nil): require req.Session == c.Descriptor.Session and len(c.Attempts) == 0, otherwise knowledge_context_changed. Then set `c.Descriptor.Session.Generation = uuid.NewString()` and `c.Descriptor.Session.NativeSessionID = ""` and fall through to the existing fresh branch: ResolveApprovedKnowledge, ValidateKnowledgeResolutionLocks, taskKnowledgeExposure on the new session (empty history), set Prepared, Phase disclosed, encodeTaskKnowledge, one SetTaskKnowledgeDelivery. Branch B (flagged, c.Prepared != nil, replay only): require p.RequestID == req.RequestID and p.RequestHash == hash, otherwise idempotency_conflict. Require c.Descriptor.Session.NativeSessionID == "" and every field except Generation and NativeSessionID equal to req.Session, otherwise knowledge_context_changed. Then run the existing replay revalidation and contribution rebuild. Branch C (unflagged): unchanged. The response already returns Session: c.Descriptor.Session, which is the fresh binding. Add an English comment that this is the only writer that changes a claimed native binding, and only before first disclosure.

Add the unexported field `droppedPriorSessionID string` to Task, with no JSON tag. encoding/json ignores unexported fields, so a claim response cannot set it. It records that this daemon's own gate dropped the bound session.

In gateResumeToReachableSession (just before `task.PriorSessionID = ""`, ~5928) and gateCodexResumeToRolloutPresence (~6091), set `task.droppedPriorSessionID = task.PriorSessionID`. No other runTask change. The prompt already carries the continuity notice through perTurnContextBlocks (prompt.go:68), and the legacy live-resume retry stays excluded for knowledge (`execOpts.Knowledge == nil`, ~7956).

(1) validateKnowledgeClaim returns `(dropped bool, err error)`. Replace the two equality clauses at 226 with `dropped := d.Session.NativeSessionID != "" && task.droppedPriorSessionID == d.Session.NativeSessionID && task.PriorSessionID == "" && opts.ResumeSessionID == ""`, and require `dropped || (d.Session.NativeSessionID == opts.ResumeSessionID && d.Session.NativeSessionID == task.PriorSessionID)`. (2) prepareKnowledgePrompt: when dropped, set request.ResumeUnavailable = true. request.Session stays the claimed stale binding. (3) validateKnowledgePreparation takes the expected session instead of reading task.KnowledgeContext.Session (251). When dropped, the response must have NativeSessionID == "", a UUID Generation different from the claimed one, and every other field equal to the claim. Otherwise it is an exact match as today. Anything else is knowledge_context_changed with no launch. (4) After validation, set `claim.Session = prepared.Session` before building the intent. The kind becomes Fresh, intent.Session.Generation is the new generation, and the observer's claim and authorize req.Session (o.prepared.Session) carry the fresh binding. validateKnowledgeIntent's Fresh rule (ResumeSessionID == "") already holds after the gate.

Assert json.Unmarshal into TaskKnowledgePrepareRequest returns nil and that re-marshaling contains `"resume_unavailable":true`. Assert an unflagged request marshals without the key, so its hash is unchanged. Assert the case alias `"Resume_Unavailable":true` is still rejected. If resume_unavailable is `true` and ignoreResumeUnavailable is false, return Session with Generation=f.freshGeneration and NativeSessionID="". Test: first := f.run(t) must complete. Then use a new task ID, PriorSessionID=first.SessionID, and PriorWorkDir=filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "collected"), a missing directory that models GC or a non-reusable scope. tests.name: TestKnowledgeUnavailableResumeRebindsFreshGeneration
tests.setup_and_assertion: Helper flaggedPrepare(t, req): marshal req, add "resume_unavailable":true, unmarshal back into protocol.TaskKnowledgePrepareRequest, and t.Fatal on error. Steps: first := f.recordSession(t, "stale-native"). CompleteTask with "stale-native". Snapshot that row's knowledge_delivery bytes. f.nextTurn. d := f.finalize(t, "stale-native") (sanity check: same generation, native "stale-native"). StartTask. p := PrepareTaskKnowledge(flaggedPrepare(f.prepareRequest(d))). Assert p.Session.NativeSessionID=="", p.Session.Generation!=first generation, all other binding fields equal d.Session, and p.Manifest contains f.candidate.CandidateID. Replaying the same request returns the same PrepareID and Session. Authorize with a descriptor copy whose Session=p.Session, observe started / native_session "fresh-native" / terminated, then CompleteTask with "fresh-native". Assert: the stale row's knowledge_delivery bytes are unchanged; the current row's claim has Descriptor.Session==p.Session and Attempts[0].BoundSessionID=="fresh-native"; GetLastTaskSession(agent, issue) returns "fresh-native". After f.nextTurn, BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim("fresh-native") returns prior "fresh-native" with Generation==p.Session.Generation, and BuildTaskKnowledgeClaim("stale-native") still returns the first generation.
tests.why_it_fails_now: flaggedPrepare's json.Unmarshal fails on the unknown field and the test stops with t.Fatal. With the flag dropped, the request is byte-identical to a resume prepare and keeps the stale binding, so no fresh generation is returned.

tests.name: TestKnowledgeUnavailableResumeRefusesUnsafeRebind
tests.setup_and_assertion: Table test, one fixture per subtest. (1) "nothing to drop": finalize(t, "") then flagged prepare. Expect a 400 invalid_knowledge_request CollaborationError and unchanged knowledge_delivery bytes. (2) "already disclosed": a stale claim, an unflagged prepare succeeds, then a flagged prepare with a new RequestID. Expect idempotency_conflict and a descriptor that still has native "stale-native". (3) "altered binding": flagged prepare with req.Session.Generation replaced. Expect knowledge_context_changed, Prepared still nil and unchanged delivery bytes.
tests.why_it_fails_now: Every subtest builds its request through flaggedPrepare, which hits t.Fatal on current code because the field does not exist on the wire type.

In §3 'Ordinary exact-session history and lifecycle', insert a paragraph before line 108 ('First launch refusal...'): "Unreachable resume: when the daemon's reachability gate drops the claimed native session (collected or locked workdir, non-reusable scope, missing session store), it sends the original binding with `resume_unavailable`. No change. A grep found no built-in skill or source map that documents the prepare request, and no UI-visible field changes.

migrations: None. No schema, SQL or sqlc change. The rebound descriptor uses only existing JSON fields inside agent_task_queue.knowledge_delivery, so no backfill or down-migration work is needed.
compatibility_and_risks: New daemon with an older server: the older server's strict decoder answers 400 invalid_knowledge_request, the daemon reports knowledge_unavailable, and the task is blocked with no disclosure and no process. That is the same outcome as today with a different reason string. Reachable resumes and fresh claims send byte-identical requests because the field is omitempty. Old daemon with a new server: the flag is never sent, so behavior is unchanged (blocked, knowledge_context_changed). The fix lands only when the daemon is upgraded; Desktop bundles the daemon and CLI daemons need the release. Server rollback after rebinds: rebound rows contain only existing fields and pass the old decodeTaskKnowledge, the old exposure rows are untouched, and the old server simply cannot perform new rebinds, which fails closed. In-flight receipts: unflagged request hashes do not change, so an original prepare stored before the upgrade replays after it. Security: exposure is recorded only at prepare and attempt time, the rebind is allowed only before the first prepare, and the history matcher keys on the descriptor native ID or BoundSessionID, so no exposure is relabeled. Fences (claim_generation, dispatched_at) are unchanged. The fresh session is resolved under the existing lock graph and authorized for every physical attempt, and its native ID is bound through the ordinary observation writer with an atomic pointer update. A knowledge_busy result rolls back rebind and disclosure together. Human-only approval and revocation are untouched. A source revoked after being exposed only in the stale session no longer blocks the fresh turn, which never sees that source, and the stale session is still revalidated if it is chosen again. Trust: the server cannot verify reachability, but a daemon falsely reporting it gets only what a fresh claim of the same task already gets. UX: the same turn runs fresh with sessionContinuityNoticeFor (issue and chat variants), and no session is retired, matching the legacy gate drop. Repeat case: if the fresh run fails before reporting a native ID, the row stays NULL and the next claim picks the stale session again. The daemon drops and rebinds again, so each input still runs, as on the legacy path. Main implementation risk: the Prepare replay branch. Branch B must check request ID and hash before any session comparison, or a lost-response replay would be refused. Validation: no code was changed in this read-only pass and no build or test was run. DB-backed service and handler tests must run against the isolated database contract, because they silently skip or fail without DATABASE_URL.
open_questions: Optional hardening for a pre-existing gap outside H2: should the observation writer refuse a native_session under a Fresh-intent attempt when that native ID is already bound in this agent's scope history? It would stop a compromised daemon from relabeling an old session under a new generation, but it adds a history read to a writer the spec keeps binding-only. Needs an owner decision.

Should gateCodexResumeToRolloutPresence also set droppedPriorSessionID? Codex is not knowledge-supported today (KnowledgeLifecycleSupported admits built-in Claude only), so setting it is harmless and keeps the two gates symmetric. The design assumes yes.
Old daemons stay blocked on new servers until upgraded. Is a release note enough? Any server-only mitigation would have to guess reachability, and I recommend none.

Should a rebind leave an audit trace? A content-free server log line (task ID, old and new generation) is safe. A persisted field would break strict decoding on an older server after rollback, so I recommend the log line only.
